what_matters.head: Cerebras rose 9.1% after OpenAI's Sam Altman called it "a close partner" in a post late Friday.
what_matters.detail: Altman was answering a SemiAnalysis report that OpenAI's new "Ultrafast" mode runs on Nvidia GPUs rather than Cerebras chips; the stock had lost nearly 20% in the week before. OpenAI was about 20% of Cerebras's revenue in the first half of 2026 (US$74.4M of US$373.5M).

what_matters.head: Elon Musk confirmed early talks with TSMC on his Terafab chip plants in Texas: "Just discussions, but something may come of it."
what_matters.detail: The talks were first reported on Friday 2 Oct by the Culpium newsletter. TSMC rose 2.8% and touched an intraday record. Intel fell 2.6%: it had been the only named process-technology partner for Terafab's Texas plants.

what_matters.head: Micron's Taiwan union strike vote closed today (6 Oct); no result was reported by 13:50 SGT.
what_matters.detail: A pass needs yes votes from more than half of all members, and gives the union a right to strike, not a date. Micron's board is reported to review Taiwan profit-sharing options on 8 Oct, US time.

latest.tape_note: The Nasdaq closed at a record, up 1.1% at 27,477; the S&P 500 rose 0.7%, within 0.3% of its summer record. Chips were mixed: Nvidia, TSMC and Broadcom rose while Intel, Micron and SanDisk fell, so SOXX ended almost flat. The 10-year yield touched 5.349%, its highest since April 2002, and closed 3bp higher at 5.31% after the services-sector prices index (ISM) rose to 74. Oil fell 1.8%; the US dollar was flat against the Singapore dollar.
